problem: Human-aware navigation (HAN) needs accurate, real-time pedestrian detection on CPU-only robots, but sliding-window CNN detection is intractable and onboard-only sensing has limited coverage. HAN cost-function formulations are also inconsistent across prior work.
motivation: Robots operating around people must respect proxemics and social rules, which requires reliable person position and velocity estimates. Cascading a cheap handcrafted detector (ACF) with a CNN could give both speed and robustness without a GPU, and external ceiling cameras extend perception beyond the onboard field of view.
key_idea: Cascade the ACF detector (proposals) with a fine-tuned VGG-16 CNN (false-positive rejection) on CPU, then feed tracked pedestrian positions into a costmap of asymmetric Gaussian human-aware constraints for A* planning.
insight: The CNN cuts ACF false positives from 1284 to 249 on INRIA while losing only 5 true positives, which improves miss rate from 16.83% to 15.13%. An ACF score threshold (40) roughly doubles speed (3.38 to 6.62 FPS on INRIA) at a small accuracy cost (MR 16.48%). Multiple external cameras keep the robot aware of people the onboard camera cannot see, e.g. when they are occluded by a couch or out of the field of view.
method: ACF+CNN cascade: ACF generates pedestrian proposals with scores, and a CNN classifies each cropped proposal as pedestrian or not, discarding false positives, with no bounding-box regression.

CNN adaptation: VGG-VD16 pre-trained on ImageNet, input reduced from 224x224 to 64x64 (feedforward 0.3619 s to 0.0485 s), FC layers re-initialized (Gaussian, variance 0.01) with 2 output classes, fine-tuned on INRIA (10 epochs, batch 100, lr 0.001, momentum 0.9).
Training data: 1237 positive GT boxes augmented by flipping and random deformation to 4948; negatives mined with a partially trained LDCF (12552 windows); 15751 train / 1749 val.
ACF score threshold: proposals below score 40 are dropped before the CNN to speed up processing.

People tracking: bounding-box bottom-center is projected to the floor plane by a homography, and NNJPDA plus per-person constant-velocity Kalman filters give position, velocity and orientation. Posture is labeled standing, walking or seated by speed (0.1 m/s) and seat areas.

HAN cost functions: asymmetric Gaussians for the personal space of walking people, circular Gaussians for standing or seated people, a visibility Gaussian behind seated people, a circular interaction-zone cost, and an overtake-by-left Gaussian. Costs are fused by max, and hand-over opens a 45-degree, 0.6 m frontal region.
Planner: A* on the ROS navigation stack costmap with layered plug-ins, replanning periodically, with high cost near obstacles.

setting.backbone: ACF (handcrafted, boosted trees) + VGG-VD16 CNN (ImageNet-pretrained, fine-tuned on INRIA, 64x64 input)
setting.model_size: VGG-16 (~138M params at standard config; adapted to 64x64 input)
setting.training_data: ImageNet pre-training (1.2M images); fine-tuned on INRIA (4948 augmented positives, ~12.5k negatives)
setting.observation: Monocular RGB from an onboard camera plus four ceiling-mounted cameras
setting.action_space: Global A* path on a 2D costmap executed by a holonomic Mecanum-drive robot (MBOT)
setting.simulator: Gazebo with ROS (simulation); real MBOT robot in a domestic indoor testbed
setting.privileged: Homography from image to floor plane computed a priori, predefined seating areas, TV state signal via home network, known map/costmap

numbers_note: Paper reports pedestrian-detection metrics (INRIA MR/FPS) and qualitative navigation experiments, not standard embodied navigation benchmark results. INRIA: ACF MR 16.83%, ACF+CNN 15.13% at 3.38 FPS; with threshold 16.48% at 6.62 FPS. Real sequences: 10.41 FPS (corridor), 9.74 FPS (MBOT) with threshold.
results: ACF+CNN lowers INRIA log-average miss rate from 16.83% (ACF alone) to 15.13%, and with score thresholding runs at about 10 FPS on real indoor sequences on CPU, versus 0.1238 FPS for single-scale exhaustive CNN search. In four real robot experiments (slalom around standing people, overtaking on the left, avoiding a TV-watching person, hand-over) the robot behaved correctly using the multi-camera detections. No quantitative navigation metrics or baseline comparisons are given.
limitations: Navigation evaluation is qualitative, with four scenarios and no quantitative metrics or baseline comparisons.
Cost-function parameters were tuned empirically by hand, and the detector was fine-tuned only on INRIA, with no extensive CNN architecture study.
Detection reaches only about 10 FPS, and the system relies on ceiling cameras with a pre-computed homography and fixed environment knowledge (seating areas).
builds_on: R-CNN pipeline (Hosang et al. / Ribeiro et al.)
Asymmetric Gaussian HAN cost functions (Kruse et al.)
